_provenance: Two independently-observed real error-path assistant messages from ~/.omp/agent/sessions/-dev-z-harness/*.jsonl, found by scanning the full local session corpus for message.stopReason == 'error'. Across the sampled corpus (~40k assistant messages), every naturally-occurring message DOES carry a 'usage' object -- omp appears to always attach the key syntactically -- but on an error-stopReason turn the object is present with every numeric field zeroed and 'contextSnapshot' is entirely absent from the message. This is the closest naturally-occurring 'missing usage' shape we could find; a HostAdapter must treat an all-zero usage + absent contextSnapshot as 'no usable context reading' just as it would treat a genuinely missing field, not as '0% context used'.

message.errorMessage: Codex error event: The usage limit has been reached (code=usage_limit_reached)
Codex error event: Your input exceeds the context window of this model. Please adjust your input and try again. (code=context_length_exceeded)

watchdog_implication: read_context() for the omp adapter must special-case stopReason == 'error' (or totalTokens == 0 with contextSnapshot absent) as an unusable reading and fall back rather than reporting a false 0% usage that would suppress a handoff trigger.
